angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 2,101,710 km at 24.46 pc = 1.15 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 95418: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 40.89 +/- 0.16 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 24.456 +/- 0.096 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 38.6031 +/- 1.1285 mas (same row, RUWE 5.99), 34.2 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 3.021 +/- 0.038 solar radii from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 95418: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.149 +/- 0.014 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 3.021 +/- 0.038 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 2,101,710 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 9377 +/- 75 K from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 95418: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 9377 +/- 75 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 95418: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 9377 +/- 75 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101)
surfaceGravitySource: log g 3.68 from 2023ApJS..266...41P; the 10 published values span log g 3.1 to 4.3, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.3% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJS..266...41P)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * bet UMa: spectral type A1IVps (2010MNRAS.403.1089P)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * bet UMa: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * bet UMa: projected rotation speed 46 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2007A&A...463..671R)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (HST/STIS Next Generation Spectral Library v2 (Heap & Lindler; MAST high-level science product), HD 95418) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
